cohort: 831 pregnant women recruited from 10 public primary care clinics in Sao Paulo, Brazil, with 757 deliveries performed in public hospitals.
finding: After adjustment for covariates, none of the socioeconomic status variables remained associated with cesarean section.
mod_finding: The chance of women undergoing cesarean section was not associated with indicators of socioeconomic status alone, but was defined in accordance with major obstetric and clinical conditions.
